entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 35 Is 35:1-10 . Continuation of the Prophecy in the Thirty-fourth Chapter. See on Is 34:1 , introduction there. 1. solitary place-- literally, "a dry place," without springs of water. A moral wilderness is meant. for them-- namely, on account of the punishment inflicted according to the preceding prophecy on the enemy; probably the blessings set forth in this chapter are included in the causes for joy ( Is 55:12 ). rose-- rather, "the meadow-saffron," an autumnal flower with bulbous roots; so Syriac translation.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8957"/><div sID="gen15060" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8957"/><hi type="bold">2. glory of Lebanon--</hi>its ornament, namely, its cedars (<reference osisRef="Isa.10.34">Is 10:34</reference>).<div eID="gen15060" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15061" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">excellency of Carmel--</hi>namely, its beauty.<div eID="gen15061" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15062" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Sharon--</hi>famed for its fertility.<div eID="gen15062" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15063" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">see ... glory of the Lord ... excellency--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.40.5">Is 40:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.40.9">9</reference>). While the wilderness which had neither "glory" nor "excellency" shall have both "given to it," the Lord shall have all the "glory" and "excellency" ascribed to Him, not to the transformed wilderness (<reference osisRef="Matt.5.16">Mt 5:16</reference>). <div eID="gen15063" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 2. glory of Lebanon-- its ornament, namely, its cedars ( Is 10:34 ). excellency of Carmel-- namely, its beauty. Sharon-- famed for its fertility. see ... glory of the Lord ... excellency-- ( Is 40:5 , 9 ). While the wilderness which had neither "glory" nor "excellency" shall have both "given to it," the Lord shall have all the "glory" and "excellency" ascribed to Him, not to the transformed wilderness ( Mt 5:16 ).

Strengthen ... hands ... confirm ... knees--</hi>The Hebrew for "strengthen" refers to the strength residing in the hand for grasping and holding a thing manfully; "confirm," to the firmness with which one keeps his ground, so as not to be dislodged by any other [Maurer]. Encourage the Jews, now desponding, by the assurance of the blessings promised. <div eID="gen15064" type="x-p"/>

The sun's rays refracted on the glowing sands at midday give the appearance of a lake of water and often deceive the thirsty traveller (compare <reference osisRef="Jer.2.13">Jr 2:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.41.18">Is 41:18</reference>).<div eID="gen15071" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15072" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">dragons--</hi>rather, "jackals."<div eID="gen15072" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15073" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">each--</hi>namely, jackal.<div eID="gen15073" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15074" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">grass--</hi>rather, "a dwelling or receptacle (answering to the previous habitation) for reeds," &c. (which only grow where there is water, <reference osisRef="Job.8.11">Job 8:11</reference>). Where once there was no water, water shall abound. <div eID="gen15074" type="x-p"/>
